弧.meaning: A violinist snaps her <part>bow</part> in the middle of a concert and grabs the nearest thing from the buffet: a slice of <part>melon</part>, curved like a smile. She saws away with the rind and the music sounds fine. The crowd cheers that bright green <kanji>arc</kanji>.
弧.on: A <sound>ko</sound>ala in the front row quietly eats the rest of the melon.

吏.meaning: On a sunny beach, a man in a peaked cap measures every sandcastle with a <part>length</part> of string before it may stand. Then he opens his loud <part>mouth</part>: 'Too tall! Permit needed!' The children groan at the beach <kanji>officer</kanji>.
吏.on: After lunch he snorkels out over the coral <sound>ree</sound>f, measuring the fish.

麓.meaning: A <part>deer</part> who hates climbing opens a café in the <part>grove</part> at the very bottom of the mountain. Hikers stop for cocoa on the way up and again on the way down, and she never has to go further uphill than her own door. Business is best at the <kanji>foothill</kanji>.
麓.on: On busy days she sends cocoa up the slope strapped to a toy <sound>rock</sound>et.
麓.kun: At closing time she rolls out a <sound>fu</sound>ton by the stove, <sound>mo</sound>ps the floor and nibbles one last <sound>to</sound>ffee.

嫡.meaning: Three strangers arrive to claim the old lighthouse. Each one climbs up and tries to light the great <part>hanging lantern</part>, and it stays dark, until a quiet <part>woman</part> from the village strikes one match and it blazes. Her grandfather built it: she's the <kanji>legitimate</kanji> heir.
嫡.on: She <sound>chuck</sound>s the spent match into the waves and waves the strangers goodbye.

賜.meaning: A panel of <part>shellfish</part> in tiny wigs sits on a rock, handing out money to young inventors. Their rule is <part>easy</part>: show them something that makes a crab laugh. A boy with a self-buttering toaster wins the biggest <kanji>grant</kanji>.
賜.on: The crabs pay him in coins piled high on a knight's <sound>shi</sound>eld.
賜.kun: '<sound>Ta</sound>-da!' the boy cries, and the head crab hands his <sound>ma</sound>ma a fat <sound>wa</sound>d of notes.

腺.meaning: A tiny explorer, shrunk to the size of a dust speck, hikes across a runner's arm under the <part>moon</part>. Every few steps a warm <part>spring</part> bubbles up out of the skin and soaks her boots. Each one is a sweat <kanji>gland</kanji>.
腺.on: She hides from the next splash behind a hair standing tall like a <sound>sen</sound>try.

迭.meaning: A pet shop moves across town. The owner wheels the fish tanks down a slippery <part>ramp</part> into the van, terrified to <part>lose</part> a single drop or fin. Every tank, snail and pond weed goes from the old shop to the new one: a delicate <kanji>transfer</kanji>.
迭.on: The last to go is one tiny <sound>tet</sound>ra fish, carried over in a teacup.

罵.meaning: A grumpy <part>horse</part> gets tangled in a tennis <part>net</part> at the park. Instead of neighing, he shouts rude names at everyone who walks past: 'Turnip nose! Soggy biscuit!' Nobody has ever heard such <kanji>abuse</kanji> from a horse.
罵.on: He even yells at the <sound>ba</sound>rbecue for blowing smoke at him.
罵.kun: '<sound>Kno</sound>ck, <sound>kno</sound>ck,' says a passing <sound>shee</sound>p, trying a joke to calm him. The horse just yells louder.

鬱.meaning: On a grey Monday, a cat hides under a <part>blanket</part> between two <part>tree</part> trunks with a <part>tin can</part> of cold beans and a dried-up <part>herb pot</part>. Its <part>whiskers</part> droop, the rain drips, the beans stay cold. Everything is <kanji>gloom</kanji>.
鬱.on: The cat sighs a long '<sound>Oo</sound>,' then sneezes at the dusty herb pot: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!'
鬱.kun: A friend brings hot soup. The cat starts a grumpy '<sound>Oo</sound>-' and stops short, like a hiccup, then takes the spoon.

錦.meaning: A pirate captain hates to give up, so when he finally must, he refuses a plain <part>white flag</part>. His crew stitches it all over with <part>gold</part> thread, dragons, waves and roses, until it's stiff and shining. The navy accepts his surrender just to stare at the <kanji>brocade</kanji>.
錦.on: A <sound>kin</sound>gfisher lands on the mast to admire it.
錦.kun: The captain bows, bangs his k<sound>nee</sound> on the rail, and hands over a <sound>shee</sound>p and a gold <sound>key</sound>.

酪.meaning: A farmer is too impatient to churn butter by hand, so she ties a tiny stick of <part>dynamite</part> to <part>each</part> milk churn and lights the fuses. Boom: butter, cream and cheese rain down on the barn. The thin, runny liquid left at the bottom is <kanji>whey</kanji>.
酪.on: She scoops up what she can and carries it home in a dripping <sound>ruck</sound>sack.

陪.meaning: A tiny emperor penguin climbs onto a <part>soapbox</part> under a fluttering <part>pennant</part> and clears his throat. Every penguin on the ice bows so low their beaks touch the snow, and he hasn't even started his speech yet. That's <kanji>obeisance</kanji>.
陪.on: His assistant follows him everywhere, pedalling a tiny <sound>bi</sound>ke across the ice.

湧.meaning: In a cold pot, the <part>water drops</part> huddle at the bottom, too scared to move. The cook gives them a pep talk, the flame gives them <part>courage</part>, and one by one they leap up, bubbling and cheering, until the lid rattles. They <kanji>boil</kanji>.
湧.on: The steam curls up into the shape of a <sound>u</sound>nicorn and gallops out of the window.
湧.kun: Then the cook stirs in a lump of <sound>wa</sound>sabi, and the pot froths right over the top.

悦.meaning: A little horned <part>imp</part> tastes a ripe strawberry for the first time. Its <part>heartbeat</part> goes wild on its fitness watch, pip-pip-pip, and it rolls on the floor kicking its legs and giggling. Pure <kanji>ecstasy</kanji>.
悦.on: It makes an <sound>etch</sound>ing of the strawberry to hang over its bed.
悦.kun: Next it tries <sound>yo</sound>gurt, shares a crumb with a <sound>ro</sound>bin and hugs a sleepy <sound>ko</sound>ala, giggling again.

謹.meaning: At a royal garden party, the gardener must give a thank-you <part>speech</part>. She's so shy that she gives it from behind a <part>potted shrub</part>, in a whisper, bowing after every few words. Nobody sees her, but the queen nods: very <kanji>discreet</kanji>.
謹.on: A <sound>kin</sound>gfisher hiding in the shrub hears every word.
謹.kun: Then she tiptoes away, sneezing tiny '<sound>tsu</sound>, <sound>tsu</sound>' sneezes into her sleeve, and hides behind a <sound>shee</sound>p.

庸.meaning: Aliens studying Earth pick the dullest garden they can find: one grey <part>shed</part>, one <part>rake</part>, one brown <part>fence</part>. They photograph it from every side, gasping with delight. To them it's treasure. To us it's <kanji>commonplace</kanji>.
庸.on: Before they fly off, they beam up a dusty <sound>yo</sound>-yo from the shed as well.

昧.meaning: A stage crew hangs a cardboard <part>sun</part> on strings for the sunrise scene, but when the curtain opens it's <part>not yet</part> there: it's stuck up in the rafters. The actors stumble about, bumping into each other in the <kanji>dark</kanji>.
昧.on: In the blackness, a crowd of <sound>mi</sound>ce scurries on and steals the show.
昧.kun: Backstage, the <sound>coo</sound>k drops a whole bowl of <sound>ra</sound>men in the gloom.

曖.meaning: The <part>sun</part> falls in <part>love</part> with the moon and slides behind it to be close. At midday the whole town goes <kanji>dark</kanji>, the birds fall silent, and nobody can tell quite what's going on.
曖.on: The moon blushes and hides its face behind a curtain of <sound>i</sound>vy.
曖.kun: Down below, a man who can't see a thing sits on a <sound>cu</sound>shion and cheers 'Hur<sound>rah</sound>!' anyway.

繭.meaning: Camping on the <part>grass</part>, a caterpillar refuses to use the tent's metal <part>frame</part>. Instead she knits her own sleeping bag out of <part>thread</part> and zips herself in up to the antennae. The other <part>insect</part> campers peek in: no tent, just a snug <kanji>cocoon</kanji>.
繭.on: The camp dog curls up in its <sound>ken</sound>nel next to her, jealous.
繭.kun: Her <sound>ma</sound>ma tucks a sprig of <sound>eu</sound>calyptus inside so it smells nice.

睦.meaning: Two old frogs sit on two little mounds of <part>soil</part> by the pond, so close their dangling <part>legs</part> touch. They gaze <part>eye</part> to eye, share flies and finish each other's croaks. Fifty years together, and still <kanji>intimate</kanji>.
睦.on: Their pet <sound>box</sound>er dog snores happily between the two mounds.
睦.kun: A cow wanders by, gives a short '<sound>Moo</sound>' and a sneeze, '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', and the frogs shuffle up to make room for her.

剛.meaning: A hiker tries to carve her name into a rocky <part>ridge</part> with a little <part>dagger</part>. The blade bends, then snaps, then her spare snaps too. The ridge doesn't have a single scratch on it. That rock is <kanji>sturdy</kanji>.
剛.on: A <sound>goa</sound>t trots along the ridge, kicking it with hard hooves, just to show off.

墾.meaning: A <part>leopard</part> who has given up hunting builds a clanking <part>robot</part> to dig up the wild <part>soil</part> at the edge of the jungle. It rips out roots and rocks, the leopard plants carrots behind it, and soon there are neat green rows. They <kanji>cultivate</kanji> new farmland.
墾.on: A <sound>con</sound>dor circles overhead, hoping the robot digs up something tasty.
墾.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' laughs the leopard, as the first carrot pops up.

嘲.meaning: Every <part>morning</part> the alarm clock rings, and every morning the parrot opens its big <part>mouth</part>, copies the ring perfectly, then cackles at the clock for being so slow. The clock can't answer back. It just has to sit there and take the <kanji>ridicule</kanji>.
嘲.on: The parrot shows off its sparkly <sound>cho</sound>ker while it laughs.
嘲.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' it squawks, then flies off to the ba<sound>za</sound>ar to buy <sound>ke</sound>tchup for its toast.

楷.meaning: A woodpecker carves letters into a <part>tree</part> for the forest's signs, and <part>all</part> the other birds check each one: straight strokes, square corners, nothing scribbled. One wobbly line and it starts again. The signs are famous for their <kanji>correctness</kanji>.
楷.on: The neatest sign of all reads: no <sound>ki</sound>te flying near this tree.

頒.meaning: The giant <part>rubber duck</part> balloon at the town parade pops, so the mayor cuts it into a thousand pieces. She stands on the town hall steps and gives one <part>part</part> to every child: a yellow scrap, a wing, a bit of beak. She loves to <kanji>hand out</kanji> souvenirs.
頒.on: Every scrap comes with a spoonful of <sound>hon</sound>ey.
頒.kun: The last scrap goes to a crying toddler, and his '<sound>Wah</sound>!' turns into a giggle.

滋.meaning: Grandma's <part>sewing kit</part> holds no needles, only dried herbs, beans and barley on little spools. She shakes some into a pan, adds <part>water drops</part> from the tap, and simmers it all day. One mug of it mends a cold better than any medicine: truly <kanji>nourishing</kanji>.
滋.on: Her grandson drinks it in his muddy <sound>jee</sound>p before driving home.

罷.meaning: A circus bear can juggle, ride a unicycle and sing: every <part>ability</part> in the book. One night the safety <part>net</part> under her tightrope is missing, so she folds her arms, hangs up her hat and walks out of the tent. She has <kanji>quit</kanji>.
罷.on: She clicks out of the big top, a tall red <sound>hee</sound>l on each foot.
罷.kun: She tells her <sound>ma</sound>ma to stay <sound>ca</sound>lm: she'll find a better circus.

鶴.meaning: A tall white <part>bird</part> moves into a little <part>birdhouse</part> on a post, but only her body fits. Her long legs dangle out of the bottom, her neck pokes out of the chimney, and she sleeps standing on one foot anyway. Too tall for any house: a <kanji>crane</kanji>.
鶴.on: In the morning she finds a fish <sound>carc</sound>ass on her roof, left by a cheeky gull.
鶴.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' she sneezes at the smell, and a <sound>roo</sound>k on the next post says bless you.

謄.meaning: An emperor who always speaks in the <part>imperial we</part> ('We are pleased...') feeds his <part>speech</part> into a clattering old machine. It cranks out a thousand smudgy purple sheets that smell of ink, one for every village. That's a <kanji>mimeograph</kanji>.
謄.on: One damp sheet sticks to his big <sound>toe</sound> as he walks away.

錮.meaning: A greedy dragon sleeps on her pile of <part>gold</part> for so long that the coins <part>harden</part> around her like a plaster cast. She can blink, but she can't move a claw. Locked inside her own treasure: total <kanji>confinement</kanji>.
錮.on: A <sound>ko</sound>ala climbs in through the window and pinches one coin a day.
錮.kun: Her <sound>foo</sound>t is stuck, and a tin of <sound>sa</sound>rdines sits just out of reach: all blocked up.
